name: 113. Vertex embedding usage and batch arity (#1587) (vertex-embedding-usage)
description:
Vertex serves embeddings from two endpoints and Bifrost picks between them by model name: gemini-embedding-2* goes to `:embedContent`, everything else to `:predict`. They report usage in different places, and only one of them was being read.

`:embedContent` returns `usageMetadata.promptTokenCount`, but `GeminiEmbeddingResponse` - shared with the Gemini provider - had no field for it, so it was dropped at unmarshal: HTTP 200, `usage: null`, and a null cost in the logs (the live half of #1587). 113.A1 pins it. 113.A2 is the control on the other endpoint, where usage comes from per-embedding `statistics.tokenCount` instead - that branch must keep working, since both now run through the same converter.

113.A3 pins the arity. `:embedContent` takes exactly one content, and Vertex offers no batch alternative for these models: `:batchEmbedContents` is 404 there, `contents[]` is rejected as an unknown field, and `:predict` answers FAILED_PRECONDITION - all verified against the live endpoint. So a batched request is a caller error and must stay a clean 400 rather than becoming a 500 or a silently truncated response. Note this is model-class specific: the same batched request to a `:predict` model returns one vector per input (53.C3). Run with FEATURE=vertex-embedding-usage.

exec: // Upstream sends usageMetadata: {promptTokenCount, promptTokensDetails, totalTokenCount}.
// A null usage here means the field was dropped at unmarshal again, which bills the request
// as zero tokens - visible as a null cost in the logs rather than as an error.
var body = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test(':embedContent model returns an embedding', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(200);
var j; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {
pm.expect.fail('response was not JSON: ' + body.slice(0, 300)); return; }
var data = j.data || [];
pm.test('one vector comes back', function () {
pm.expect(data.length, 'wrong vector count; body: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(1);
pm.expect(Array.isArray(data[0].embedding), 'embedding is not an array').to.be.true;
pm.expect(data[0].embedding.length, 'embedding is empty').to.be.above(0);
pm.test('usage is carried through from usageMetadata', function () {
pm.expect(j.usage, 'usage missing entirely - usageMetadata was dropped at unmarshal').to.be.an('object');
pm.expect(j.usage.prompt_tokens, 'prompt_tokens is 0/absent; this request bills as free').to.be.above(0);
pm.expect(j.usage.total_tokens, 'total_tokens is 0/absent').to.be.above(0);

item.name: 113.A2 vertex/text-embedding-005 - :predict usage still comes from statistics - #1587

exec: // Control for 113.A1. This endpoint reports no usageMetadata; usage is summed from each
// prediction's statistics.tokenCount. Both paths share one converter, so the usageMetadata
// branch must not have shadowed this one.
var body = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test(':predict model returns an embedding', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'failed: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(200);
var j; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {
pm.expect.fail('response was not JSON: ' + body.slice(0, 300)); return; }
var data = j.data || [];
pm.test('one vector comes back', function () {
pm.expect(data.length, 'wrong vector count; body: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(1);
pm.expect(Array.isArray(data[0].embedding), 'embedding is not an array').to.be.true;
pm.test('usage is populated from per-embedding statistics', function () {
pm.expect(j.usage, 'usage missing entirely').to.be.an('object');
pm.expect(j.usage.prompt_tokens, 'prompt_tokens is 0/absent - the statistics branch regressed').to.be.above(0);
pm.expect(j.usage.total_tokens, 'total_tokens is 0/absent').to.be.above(0);

item.name: 113.A3 [EXPECT-4XX] vertex/gemini-embedding-2-preview - batch input is a clean 400 - #1587

exec: // Verified against the live endpoint: Vertex has no batch shape for this model class.
//   :embedContent with contents[]  -> 400 Unknown name "contents"
//   :batchEmbedContents            -> 404 (endpoint does not exist on Vertex)
//   :predict (1 or 2 instances)    -> 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION
// So the rejection belongs to the caller, and must be raised before the provider call rather
// than surfacing as a 5xx or a response quietly covering only the first input. 53.C3 is the
// contrast: the same batched request to a :predict model returns one vector per input.
var body = pm.response.text() || '';
pm.test('batch input is rejected with 400', function () {
pm.expect(pm.response.code, 'expected 400; body: ' + body.slice(0, 300)).to.eql(400);
var j; try { j = pm.response.json(); } catch (e) {
pm.expect.fail('response was not JSON: ' + body.slice(0, 300)); return; }
pm.test('the error explains the arity and no partial result came back', function () {
var message = ((j.error || {}).message) || '';
pm.expect(message.toLowerCase(), 'error does not explain the arity: ' + JSON.stringify(j).slice(0, 300))
.to.include('batch');
pm.expect((j.data || []).length, 'a vector came back alongside the rejection').to.eql(0);
